title: Prompting fundamentals
description: Instructions, roles, few-shot examples and chain-of-thought as ways to condition a next-token predictor; prompts as testable artifacts.

title: Self-consistency and tree-of-thought
description: Sampling several reasoning paths and voting on the final answer; the binomial accuracy gain and its independence caveat; search over thoughts.

title: Structured outputs and constrained decoding
description: JSON Schema as a contract, token-level masking with a grammar automaton, validation and repair loops.

title: Function calling and tool protocols
description: The model emits a structured call, application code executes it, the result returns to the context; schemas, errors and loop limits.

title: Context engineering
description: Budgeting the context window, ordering and recency effects, compaction, retrieval versus long context.

title: Prefix caching and cost
description: Provider-side prefix caches, cache-friendly prompt layout, write premium versus read discount and break-even reuse.

title: Evaluating LLM applications
description: Eval sets, rubrics, LLM-as-judge pitfalls, regression gates and statistical comparison of two prompts.

title: Guardrails and application safety
description: Layered input and output filters, PII detection with checksum validators, prompt-injection defence, rate limits and fallbacks.

title: Production LLM architecture
description: Gateway, orchestration, retrieval, tools and observability; latency and cost budgeting.

title: Agent loops as state machines, and MCP
description: Explicit graph of nodes and edges with reducers, checkpoints and interrupts; the Model Context Protocol as a shared tool interface.
